result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, and PollFeed's execute opens and parses the whole feed (open + SimpleRSS.parse + TopicEmbed.import per item) before fetch_http. This runs on the user-triggered RetrieveTopic path, so a user embedding an article incurs a full feed poll inline, and concurrent requests can trigger overlapping polls that race on the same feed items (TopicEmbed.import does check for existing embeds but only at read time, so races are plausible). This is a concrete scope/architecture concern grounde

judged_text: perform_retrieve synchronously runs the entire feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) inside the per-URL RetrieveTopic job, duplicating the scheduler's responsibility on a user-triggered path. Every embed of a not-yet-imported article re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed inline (open + parse + one topic per item), so the requesting user's article appears only after the full poll finishes, and N users embedding different articles concurrently run N overlapping full polls that race on the same feed items.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (new file `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) conditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. This means each per-URL retrieval path (triggered via `EmbedController#best` enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) can synchronously poll and parse the entire feed (`open` + `SimpleRSS.parse` + iterating all `rss.items` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). That duplicates the scheduled job’s responsibility and can cause redundant work / contention when multiple retrieve jobs run concurrently. This is an architecture/performance concern grounded in the diff rather than a definite functional defect.
